subject: Running Revo R in Linux MLK not performng as expected

messages.author: b06181dd1b34df5a
messages.subject: Running Revo R in Linux MLK not performng as expected
parts: Good morning everyone. I am a statistician running a mixed model using Revo R, Linux system. 399 variables, 1600 random effects and a large number of records. I was expecting a better performance of Revo R compared to single thread R. (I tried the model using a small chunk of data). My IT person checked the threads my job was using using a ps command in Linux. He said he noticed that only 2 were used out of 16 I have access to. I only got a reduction of 5 minutes using Revo R compared to R.  Am I doing something wrong?  any suggestions will be appreciated. -Breda

messages.author: 0eb5a09fd4de9e5e
messages.subject: Re: Running Revo R in Linux MLK not performng as expected
parts:
Can you please provide a bit more detail, e.g. which packages and functions you are using?

(In the ideal case, please provide a reproducible example that allows us to test and replicate what you are doing.)

Note that the Intel MKL will only accelerate and parallelize matrix computations. If your lme algorithm does not make heavy use of matrix algebra, then you may not see much of a difference.

Andie

messages.author: 0eb5a09fd4de9e5e
messages.subject: Re: [RRO] Re: Running Revo R in Linux MLK not performng as expected
parts:
Hi, Breda
 
Thank you for the additional information. Reading the code, I can see that glmmPQL uses MASS::mle() under the hood. The functionlme() uses some matrix computation, including crossprod() so the MKL should help you here, as you say.
 
In RRO, you can set the number of threads using this code:
 
library(RevoUtilsMath)
setMKLthreads(8)
  
You can query how many threads are in use with:
 
getMKLthreads()
 
Also, can you please tell us what hardware you are using, as well as which operating system?

Andrie
